title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers an adapter's request with, application/json. The codes an adapter meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking: a missing signature, or one that is not 64 bytes of strict base64url; a well-formed signature that fails to verify, an S at or above the group order included; a missing or malformed access key id; an unknown or revoked access key, or a key of another kind; a GET's X-Qory-Timestamp that is missing, not a decimal integer, or more than 300 seconds from the control plane's clock, either way; a POST's time more than 300 seconds from it, either way; and a replay, a request whose signature it has already seen, under the replay rule of definitions.schema.json. It tells the adapter nothing about which cause applied, and an adapter never takes it as the access key being revoked; 403 forbidden, a request outside the access key's rights, or naming a connection_id that is unknown, that belongs to another adapter, or, in a listing of collections, that is not yet made (pending), with the same signed body for every cause: when the control plane no longer holds a connection, as after its organisation is removed, it answers 403, not connection_ended, so an adapter treats a 403 that lasts after its retries, on any request for a connection whose listing the control plane has accepted once, answered 204, whether a listing, items, comments or a disconnect, as the connection ended, and drops that connection's collections from its state, as on 409 connection_ended, choosing how many retries and over what time; a pending link, one with no listing ever accepted, is never dropped by counting 403s, since its listing is refused 403 by design until the person's browser delivers the connect return, and the adapter drops it once the connect return it minted for it has expired, or when a new pass replaces it; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 collection_not_linked, items of a collection that is not linked to a workspace; 409 connection_ended, a request of a connection that ended, or for a collection of one, final for that connection: the adapter drops that connection's collections from its state; 409 connection_suspended, a request of a connection whose organisation is out of use for now, or for a collection of one, not final: the adapter changes no state and sends the request again on its periodic check; the control plane decides 403 first, then connection_ended, then connection_suspended, and both before collection_not_linked, except on POST /v1/connections/disconnect, where the order is 403, then connection_ended, and connection_suspended does not apply: a disconnect of a suspended connection is answered with the signed 204 and ends the connection; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the adapter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as definitions.schema.json describes a retry. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the adapter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the adapter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A signed answer is signed as definitions.schema.json describes. A member this schema does not define is refused.
